answer:
The changelog shows that Python 3.9 has been deprecated, but the excerpts don't say when it will be removed or whether any package has already dropped it. Several packages in the March 2026 releases list the same change:

"chore: deprecate python 3.9 once and for all ([#20956](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/pull/20956))" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/CHANGELOG.md]

This entry appears under llama-index-instrumentation 0.5.0 (2026-03-16), llama-index-embeddings-litellm 0.5.0, llama-index-embeddings-llamafile 0.5.0, and llama-index-embeddings-autoembeddings 0.3.0 (2026-03-12), among others.

For context, the earlier change was dropping Python 3.8 support, which is a different version: "Dropped python3.8 support, Unpinned numpy (#16973)" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/CHANGELOG.md], in the llama-index-core 0.12.0 release from 2024-11-17.

I don't know the exact end-of-support date for Python 3.9 or whether any package currently still installs or tests on it. Checking the package's release notes or metadata would answer that.
